# ANALYSIS: Orchestrator Pattern Change for Long-Running Compute

**Filed:** 2026-09-11
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)
**Type:** quality_gate
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

By changing the orchestrator pattern to have workers perform synchronous smoke-testing (foreground, timeout <=10min) and the orchestrator manage background processes end-to-end, we eliminate orphaned runs and improve compute reliability. This ensures long-running tasks do not leave processes consuming resources indefinitely.

## Mechanism

Workers: Execute script build and smoke-test synchronously in foreground with Bash timeout <=10min. Return immediately after smoke test (pass/fail). Do not launch long-running processes.

Orchestrator: Launches actual long-running compute in background, polls process status, owns full lifecycle (start, monitor, terminate on completion/failure, resource cleanup). No process runs without orchestrator supervision.

   - Blow-up scenario: Orchestrator bug causing premature termination or launch failure → disrupted compute tasks.

## Pre-merge gate

- Orchestrator must pass tests for background process launch, polling, termination, and resource cleanup.
- Workers must pass tests for synchronous smoke-test execution with <=10min timeout and appropriate exit codes.
- Integration tests must confirm zero orphaned runs post-worker completion.
- Trading strategy validators (gym, walk-forward, real-fills) remain unaffected but must still pass for any strategy using the orchestrator.

## Confidence

9 / 10 -- The pattern cleanly separates concerns: workers handle quick validation and exit, orchestrator manages long-running processes. This is a proven anti-orphan pattern in distributed systems.

This change is orthogonal to all trading strategy candidates. It alters no trading logic, so leaderboard impact is null. It complements all candidates by providing reliable compute infrastructure for backtests/grinders.
